question: Is a GENEROUS wall timeout + AGGRESSIVE RLIMIT_CPU CPU-time budget more robust against SPURIOUS timeouts under host CPU contention than today's tight wall-only timeout in safe-ci-dag-runner?

method.victim_work: awk summing 64,000,000 ints ~= 2.0 CPU-seconds (~2.25s idle boxed wall)
method.load_model: N extra concurrent CPU-bound steps in the SAME DAG (sibling step-*.cpu cgroups), whole runner pinned to core 0 via taskset -c 0 so K concurrent equal steps each get ~1/K of the core (wall inflates ~Kx, CPU-s fixed)
method.why_load_inside_dag: the runner boxes each step in its own cgroup-v2 scope, so EXTERNAL-slice host load barely slows a step; the wall flakes that bite CI come from contention AMONG the runner's own concurrent steps

policies.wall-tight: timeout=4s (~1.5x over 2.25s idle boxed wall), cpu_timeout=0 (wall-only == today)
policies.cpu-generous: timeout=120s (generous wall backstop), cpu_timeout=6 CPU-s (~3x the ~2 CPU-s of real work)

method.flake_definition: any non-PASS on the fixed ~2 CPU-s of LEGITIMATE victim work

runaway_control: infinite busy-loop under cpu-generous (6 CPU-s budget, 120s wall backstop) is KILLED at ~6 CPU-s via CPU-TIMEOUT (RLIMIT_CPU), NOT allowed to run to the 120s wall -> robustness, not mere leniency
interpretation: The load-invariant CPU-time budget eliminates the wall-timeout flake (100% -> 0% at moderate/swamped) while still bounding a genuine runaway. Confirms the owner's CPU-time approach.
reproduction: RUNNER=<release binary path> ./run.sh  (raw logs land in ignored/, tracked outputs in results/)
